annotations.title: Change a document by its link

description: Writes a new version of a document by its link — e.g. the person asks in the chat to remove something on page 2 — and prints it again: the PDF link, the same edit link (the editor open on it shows the change). The new version replaces the one before. A change of a few places: edits — each replaces one exact piece of the source as get_document returned it (cheaper than sending the whole document, and nothing else moves); a rewrite: the whole new html. With base_revision: a document the person changed after you read it is refused, so read it again.

base_revision.description: The revision you read (get_document, or the last result). Required: a document the person changed after it is refused, never overwritten.

data.description: The template's new data. Alone, only for a template (kind "template"); with html, non-empty data makes the document a template. Omitted: the data stays.

edits.description: Changes to the source instead of the whole html, applied in order, all or none: each old_str is text copied exactly from the source (get_document, at base_revision) and must occur in it exactly once — add surrounding text to make it unique; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it).

filename.description: A new PDF file name, kept for its later prints. Default: the name it was printed with (render_pdf filename), else its <title>.

html.description: The whole new source. Omitted: the source stays (e.g. new data only). Not with edits.

pdf_a.description: Declare PDF/A (Pro and Max plans): "3a" — ISO 19005-3 level A, tagged, includes PDF/UA-1 (archive and accessibility at once); "1b" — ISO 19005-1 level B (PDF 1.4: transparency flattened into images). A document that cannot conform is refused with the reason. Kept for the document's later prints; "none" declares none. Omitted: the document's setting stays.

pdf_ua.description: The PDF/UA part the file declares: 1 (ISO 14289-1, PDF 1.7) — every print declares it; 2 (ISO 14289-2, PDF 2.0; Pro and Max plans). Not with pdf_a. Kept for the document's later prints; 1 returns to the default. Omitted: the document's setting stays.

preview.description: Pictures (PNG) of pages come with the answer, so you can check the layout, fonts and images before giving the links. Default: true.

preview_pages.description: Which pages to see, 1-based; -1 is the last page. Default: page 1 and the last page (a page that spilled over shows there). Up to 4, e.g. [1, 2, -1]. Every answer has the outline: which heading starts on which page.

shrink_to_fit.description: Print a document wider than its page smaller, to fit, as a browser's print does: every length then prints scaled down. Default: false, lengths print at their size (20mm is 20mm). Prefer fitting the layout to the page; use this for a page made for a screen. Kept for the document's later prints. Omitted: the document's setting stays.

name: update_document

documentId.description: The document, for get_document and update_document.

editUrl.description: The document in the ReflowPDF editor: the person edits it there (the link is the document; it lasts while it is used).

guest.description: Printed without an account: the pages carry the ReflowPDF mark.

mark.description: Whether the PDF carries the ReflowPDF mark, and why.

missingFonts.description: Font families the document named that no face answered: their text took the next family of its list.

missingVariables.description: Template values the data did not have (printed empty).

notes.description: Facts about this PDF: how long its link works, its mark, what was not fetched or filled.

outline.description: The document's headings (h1–h6, the PDF's bookmarks) in order, each with the page it starts on: pick preview_pages by it.

paper.description: Its paper, e.g. "A4", "Letter", "210 × 99 mm"; empty when unknown.

pdfUrl.description: The PDF (the same link as url).

preview.description: Which pages came with this answer as pictures (PNG), or why none did.

previews.description: Pages as pictures (PNG), kept with the PDF for its day.

renderMs.description: How long the print took on the server, in milliseconds (the engine and its adapter).

revision.description: Its revision: name it to update_document as base_revision.

skippedResources.description: Images, fonts or style sheets the server could not fetch.

standards.description: What the PDF declares, read from its file: pdfUa (its PDF/UA part) and pdfA (its PDF/A part and level, e.g. "3a"), null when it declares none.

timing.description: The engine's own parts of it, when it states them: layoutMs (styles, layout and pagination) and writeMs (writing the PDF).
